## The question

[What is the best practice to declare a tikzpicture as a math symbol?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/737348/what-is-the-best-practice-to-declare-a-tikzpicture-as-a-math-symbol), asked by [Explorer](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/322482/explorer) on TeX Stack Exchange (2025-02-17; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> My problem is a bit similar to [this link][q-1], as the following MWE:
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{tikz,amsmath}
> \usetikzlibrary{calc}
> \begin{document}
> \makeatletter
> \def\pgfgetnodeheight(#1)#2{
>   \path ($(#1.south) - (#1.north)$);
>   \pgfmathsetmacro#2{veclen(\pgf@x, \pgf@y)}
>   \edef#2{#2pt}
> }
> \def\pgfgetnodewidth(#1)#2{
>   \path ($(#1.east) - (#1.west)$);
>   \pgfmathsetmacro#2{veclen(\pgf@x, \pgf@y)}
>   \edef#2{#2pt}
> }
> \makeatother
> \DeclareRobustCommand{\notleftrightarrow}{%
>     \mathrel{\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=-.5ex]%
>         \node[inner sep=0pt,outer sep=0pt] (a) {$\Longleftrightarrow$};
>         \pgfgetnodewidth(a)\nWidth
>         \pgfgetnodeheight(a)\nHeight
>         \draw[line width=.5pt](-.6*\nHeight,-.25*\nWidth)--(.6*\nHeight,.25*\nWidth);
>       \end{tikzpicture}%
>     }\kern-1em%%
> }
> \[
> \sum_{k}^{n}f(k)%
> \fbox{%
> \begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=-.5ex]%
> \fbox{%
>   \node[inner sep=0pt,draw] (a) {$\Longleftrightarrow$};%
>   \pgfgetnodewidth(a)\nWidth%
>   \pgfgetnodeheight(a)\nHeight%
>   \fbox{%
>     \draw[line width=.5pt](-.6*\nHeight,-.25*\nWidth)--(.6*\nHeight,.25*\nWidth);
>   }
>   \fill[red] (a) circle[radius=1pt];
> }
> \end{tikzpicture}}%\mkern-15mu%
> ABC
> \]
>
> \[
> \sum_{k}^{n}f(k) \notleftrightarrow ABC
> \]
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> ![the result of the MWE[2]][q-2]
>
> ## The main purpose of this post is searching for a general method to construct a math symbol(well both vertically and horizontally aligned) with a `tikzpicture`:
>
> So, I have two questions:
>
> 1. why there exists starnge space after the `node` inside the `tikzpicture`, how to tune the code here?
>
> 2. To turn a tikzpicture into a math symbol(which could change the four styles with `mathchoice`), is the solution of John Kormylo with `\tempdima` always the **best practice**?
> I wonder whether if the `amsmath` or `mathtools` provide more powerful commands to deal with the space problem in this case better?
>
> ```latex
> \DeclareRobustCommand{\myop}{%
>   \mathbin{\text{\settoheight{\tempdima}{\mathstrut}\raisebox{-.3\tempdima}{%
>     \tikz{\draw[line width=0.05\tempdima] circle (0.6\tempdima);
>     \node[scale=0.8] {$r$};}}}}}
> ```
>

> ## Editted Version of `egreg`'s comment about `centernot`:
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
> \usepackage{centernot}
> \makeatletter
> \newcommand*{\mycenternot}{%
>     \mathpalette\@mycenternot
> }
> \def\@mycenternot#1#2{%
>     \mathrel{%
>         \rlap{%
>                 \settowidth\dimen@{$\m@th#1{#2}$}%
>                 \kern.5\dimen@
>                 \settowidth\dimen@{$\m@th#1=$}%
>                 \kern-.5\dimen@
>                 $\m@th#1\slash$%<-%
>             }%
>         {#2}%
>     }%
> }
> \makeatother
> \begin{document}
>
> $\not$
>
> $/$
>
> $\char 92$%
>
> $\backslash$
>
> $\slash$
>
> $A \centernot{\Longleftrightarrow} B$  
>
> $A \mycenternot{\Longleftrightarrow} B$
>
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> Actually, the `centernot` package use only 14 lines of code to achieve the center `\not` function, however, if I want to take the advantage of the `\not` inside the original code, it seemed not centered as below:
>
> [![the modification of centernot package][q-3]][q-3]
>

> ## Try Matthew Leingang's youth's solution, but I still found that not properly aligned the `$\Longleftrightarrow$` inside the `node`(the same case as the first-post):
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> % https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/7032/good-way-to-make-textcircled-numbers/7047#7047
> \usepackage{tikz}
> \usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
> \newcommand{\mynot}[1]{%
>     \setbox0=\hbox{$#1$}%
>     \dimen0\wd0%
>     \divide\dimen0 by 2%
>     \dimen1\ht0%
>     \divide\dimen1 by 2%
>     \begin{tikzpicture}%
>         \useasboundingbox (-\the\dimen0,-\the\dimen1) rectangle (\the\dimen0,\the\dimen1);
>         \node[outer sep=1pt,inner sep=.1ex,draw] (a) {$#1$};
>         \fill [red] circle[radius=1pt];
>         \draw[line width=.5pt](-.6*\the\dimen1,-.25*\the\dimen0)--(.6*\the\dimen1,.25*\the\dimen0);
>     \end{tikzpicture}
> }
> \begin{document}
> \[
>     xyz \mynot{\Longleftrightarrow} zyx
> \]
> \[
>     ABC \mynot{\Longleftrightarrow} CBA
> \]
> \[
>     ABC \mynot{\leftrightsquigarrow} CBA
> \]
> \end{document}
> ```

> ## Editted Version of schtandard's comments on `ooalign`, which I think is a good method for alignment:
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{amsart}
> \usepackage{amssymb}
> \usepackage{tikz}
> \usetikzlibrary{ducks}
> \makeatletter
> \newcommand*{\mynot}[2]{%
>     \mathrel{\ooalign{%
>     $\m@th{#1}$\cr\hidewidth$\m@th{#2}$\hidewidth\cr
>     }}%
> }%
> \makeatother
> \begin{document}
>
> \[
> A \Longleftrightarrow B
> \]
>
> \[
> A \leftrightsquigarrow B
> \]
>
> \[
> A \mynot{\slash}{\Longleftrightarrow} B
> \]
>
> \[
> A \mynot{\backslash}{\leftrightsquigarrow} B
> \]
>
> \[
> A \mynot{\tikz[scale=.1]{\duck[witch=black!50!gray,
> longhair=red!80!black,
> jacket=black!50!gray,
> magicwand]}}{\leftrightsquigarrow} B
> \]
>
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> [![the case with ooalign][q-7]][q-7]
>
> However, I still found that the length between the `\mynot` and the other math symbol inside is not easily to control.
>

I submit that declaring a TikZ picture as a math symbol is an [anti-pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-pattern). Leave font design to the font designers and use typography commands to make composite symbols.

[I may have dabbled in this practice](https://tex.stackexchange.com/a/7047/1402) in my youth (well, I was not young 15 years ago either), but the linked question is a good use case. The CW answer from the OP weighs the pros and cons of several make-a-symbol implementations. 

If you want something parametrizable that uses colors and variable sizes, then TikZ is the way. But if you want something that works in running math text, use an existing symbol or combination of glyphs.
